extracted.intended_audience: regulated entities and interested public (fractional aircraft owners/operators, air carriers, lenders, banks, covered financial institutions, broker-dealers) and other stakeholders who may comment on PRA information collections
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Register notices inviting public comment on renewals of information collections under the Paperwork Reduction Act and summarizing regulatory requirements for affected regulated entities (FAA fractional ownership and aviation insurance applicants; OCC flood-hazard loan requirements; FinCEN correspondent-account rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Comments Invited — PRA information collection aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: You are asked to comment on any aspect of this information collection, including (a) Whether the proposed collection of information is necessary for [the agency]’s performance; (b) the accuracy of the estimated burden; (c) ways for [the agency] to enhance the quality, utility and clarity of the information collection; and (d) ways that the burden could be minimized without reducing the quality of the collected information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each agency repeated this template (FAA, OCC, etc.) and requests comments within specified deadlines and via specified submission methods (e.g., www.reginfo.gov, email addresses, mail). Comments will be part of the public record and summarized in OMB submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 14 CFR part 91, subpart K (Fractional Aircraft Ownership)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each fractional ownership program manager and each fractional owner must comply with the requirements of 14 CFR part 91, subpart K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information collected from fractional ownership programs is used to determine if these entities are operating in accordance with the minimum safety standards of these regulations; respondents include fractional ownership operators and owners; estimated burdens and respondent counts are provided (e.g., Estimated Average Burden per Response: 1 hour, 20 minutes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aviation Insurance application and update requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Air carriers applying for FAA aviation insurance must submit an initial application and provide business information, aircraft to be covered, information about commercial insurance policies, and ongoing updates (including any changes to the initial application information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must submit required materials electronically via a web-based system; as a condition of coverage, carriers must submit any changes, provide a copy of current commercial insurance policy on an ongoing basis, and supply information for any new aircraft to be added. Estimated burdens: initial application—4 hours; policy submission—10 minutes; updates vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12 CFR 22.3 — Requirement to Purchase Flood Insurance Where Available; acceptance of private policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Under § 22.3(c)(3), national banks and Federal savings associations have the discretion to accept a flood insurance policy issued by a private insurer that is not issued under the NFIP and does not meet the definition of private flood insurance if, among other things, the policy provides sufficient protection of the designated loan and the bank or savings association has documented its conclusion regarding sufficiency of the protection in writing. Under § 22.3(c)(4)(v), banks may accept a private policy issued by a mutual aid society if coverage provides sufficient protection and the bank documents its conclusion in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Banks must evaluate sufficiency consistent with general safety and soundness principles and keep written documentation of the conclusion accepting non-NFIP/private policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12 CFR 22.5 — Escrow Requirements for Flood Insurance Premiums and Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: With certain exceptions (types of loans and size of institution), national banks, Federal savings associations, and servicers must escrow flood insurance premiums and fees for all loans secured by properties located in a Special Flood Hazard Area made, increased, extended, or renewed on or after January 1, 2016.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When escrow is required, the bank must mail or deliver a written notice informing the borrower that escrow is required. If a bank no longer qualifies for an exception, in certain cases the bank must provide written notice informing the borrower of the option to escrow all premiums and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12 CFR 22.6(a) — Required Use of Standard Flood Hazard Determination Form
rubrics_metrics.description: A national bank or Federal savings association must use the Standard Flood Hazard Determination Form developed by FEMA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory form for determining flood hazard status of collateral for loans.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12 CFR 22.6(b) — Retention of Standard Flood Hazard Determination Form
rubrics_metrics.description: A national bank or Federal savings association must retain a copy of the completed Standard Flood Hazard Determination Form for the period the bank or savings association owns the loan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention is tied to the period of loan ownership; banks must keep the completed form as documentary evidence of determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12 CFR 22.7 — Notice of Forced Placement of Flood Insurance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a bank or its loan servicer determines that the property securing the loan is not covered by adequate flood insurance, the bank/servicer must notify the borrower that the borrower should obtain adequate flood insurance coverage at the borrower’s expense in an amount at least equal to the minimum amount required under the regulation for the remaining term of the loan. If the borrower fails to purchase insurance, the bank or servicer must purchase insurance on the borrower’s behalf and may charge the borrower for premiums and fees. The insurance provider must be notified to terminate any insurance purchased by an institution or servicer within 30 days of receipt of confirmation of a borrower’s existing flood insurance coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Banks must follow specified notice and forced-placement procedures; termination of forced-placed coverage requires confirmation of borrower coverage and prompt notification to insurer.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12 CFR 22.9(a)-(b) — Borrower Notice Content for Loans in SFHAs
rubrics_metrics.description: A bank making, increasing, extending, or renewing a loan secured by property in a special flood hazard area must provide a written notice to the borrower and loan servicer that includes: a warning that the property is located in a special flood hazard area; a description of the flood insurance purchase requirements; a statement indicating that flood insurance is available under the NFIP, where applicable; a statement that similar coverage may be available from private insurers; encouragement to compare NFIP and private policies; and a statement whether Federal disaster relief assistance may be available in the event of a declared Federal flood disaster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must be comprehensive and cover all required informational elements so borrowers can make informed decisions between NFIP and private insurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12 CFR 22.9(d)-(e) — Record of Receipt of Notice and Alternate Method
rubrics_metrics.description: A bank must retain a record of the receipt of the borrower notices by the borrower and the loan servicer for the period the bank owns the loan. In lieu of providing the borrower notice, a bank may obtain a satisfactory written assurance from a seller or lessor that the seller or lessor provided such notice to the purchaser or lessee within a reasonable time before sale/lease completion; the bank must retain that written assurance for the period it owns the loan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping obligations are explicit; alternate compliance via written assurance from seller/lessor is allowed but must be retained.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12 CFR 22.10 — Notices to FEMA of Loan Servicer Identity and Servicer Transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: A bank making, increasing, extending, renewing, selling, or transferring a loan secured by property in a special flood hazard area must notify the Administrator of FEMA (or designee) of the identity of the loan servicer (notice of servicer), and must notify FEMA of any change in the loan servicer (notice of servicer transfer) within 60 days after the effective date of such change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Banks must provide timely notifications to FEMA regarding servicer identity and transfers to ensure FEMA has current servicer information.

rubrics_metrics.name: 31 CFR 1010.630(a)(1) — Prohibition on Correspondent Accounts for Foreign Shell Banks
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered financial institution is prohibited from establishing, maintaining, administering, or managing correspondent accounts in the United States for, or on behalf of, foreign shell banks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A foreign shell bank is defined as a foreign bank without a physical presence in any country. Covered financial institutions may provide correspondent accounts to foreign shell banks that qualify as 'regulated affiliates' per exceptions in the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 31 CFR 1010.630 — Reasonable steps to prevent indirect use by foreign shell banks
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered financial institution must take reasonable steps to ensure that any correspondent account established, maintained, administered, or managed in the United States for a foreign bank is not being used by that foreign bank to indirectly provide banking services to a foreign shell bank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation requires affirmative due diligence/reasonable steps by covered financial institutions to prevent indirect provision of services to shell banks.

rubrics_metrics.name: 31 CFR 1010.630(a)(2) — Record retention identifying owners and US agent for foreign banks
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered financial institution that maintains a correspondent account in the United States for a foreign bank must retain records in the United States identifying: (i) the owners of each such foreign bank whose shares are not publicly traded, unless the foreign bank files a Form FR Y-7 identifying current owners; and (ii) the name and street address of a person who resides in the United States and is authorized, and has agreed, to be an agent to accept service of legal process for records regarding each such account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners are defined (e.g., persons who directly or indirectly own/control 25% or more of voting securities). Records must be kept in the U.S. and are required unless specific alternative filings (FR Y-7) exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: 31 CFR 1010.630(b) — Certification/Recertification compliance option (every three years)
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered financial institution will be deemed in compliance if it obtains, at least once every three years, a certification or recertification from the foreign bank. FinCEN has developed an optional form that a covered financial institution may use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of the optional 'Certification Regarding Correspondent Accounts for Foreign Banks' (OMB Control Number 1506-0043) is permitted. Certification/recertification intervals and an optional form simplify compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 31 CFR 1010.630(c) — Requirement to request verification/correction if information suspected inaccurate
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered financial institution must request that a foreign bank verify or correct the information provided in a certification/recertification if the covered financial institution knows, suspects, or has reason to suspect that such information is incorrect or no longer accurate. The covered institution may take other appropriate measures to ascertain accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must be proactive about accuracy and may use interim verification measures; there are timelines tied to subsequent closure obligations if verification is not obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: 31 CFR 1010.630(d) — Account-closure and timing requirements when certification/documentation not obtained
rubrics_metrics.description: If a covered financial institution has not obtained a certification/recertification, or otherwise obtained documentation needed for certification/recertification, within 30 calendar days after the date the account is established, and at least once every three years thereafter, the covered institution must close all such foreign bank's correspondent accounts within a commercially reasonable time, and must restrict the foreign bank’s ability to establish any new position or execute any new transactions through any such account other than those transactions necessary to close the account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If interim verification pursuant to 1010.630(c) has not obtained verification within 90 calendar days after undertaking the interim verification, the institution must follow the same closure procedures. Timelines: 30 days after establishment for initial documentation; 90 days for interim verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: 31 CFR 1010.630(d)(4)-(5) — Prohibition on re-establishing closed accounts and liability safe-harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered financial institutions are prohibited from re-establishing any account closed pursuant to 1010.630(d) and from establishing any other correspondent account with the foreign bank whose account was closed unless the foreign bank provides the appropriate certification or recertification. A covered financial institution will not be held liable to any person in court or arbitration for terminating a correspondent account in accordance with 1010.630(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule creates both a restriction on reopening/establishing new accounts with the same foreign bank and a liability protection for compliant account closures.

rubrics_metrics.name: 31 CFR 1010.630(e) — Document retention requirement for original documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered financial institutions must retain any original document provided by a foreign bank, and the original or a copy of any document otherwise relied upon for compliance with 1010.630, for at least five years after the date that the institution no longer maintains any correspondent account for such foreign bank, or longer if directed by the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention of originals/copies is mandatory for a minimum five-year period after relationship termination; longer retention if Treasury/Secretary directs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to 31 CFR 1010.630 (covered financial institution, correspondent account, foreign shell bank, owner)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key definitions appear in the notice: 'covered financial institution' (entities listed in 31 U.S.C. 5312(a)(2) and related regulations), 'correspondent account' (account established for a foreign bank to receive deposits, make payments, or handle other transactions), 'foreign shell bank' (foreign bank without a physical presence in any country), and 'owner' (person owning, controlling, or able to vote 25%+ of voting securities or controlling election of majority of directors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice lists statutory/regulatory cross-references and explains which entities are encompassed by the rule; these definitions determine scope of duties and recordkeeping obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Optional Certification Form and OMB control renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: FinCEN has developed an optional form 'Certification Regarding Correspondent Accounts for Foreign Banks' (OMB Control Number 1506-0043) that covered financial institutions may use in obtaining certification/recertification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice renews the OMB control number and indicates that the collection is a renewal without change; the optional form is available at FinCEN's website. Frequency of use is 'as required' with an estimated universe of potential respondents.
